issues.t: Harsh or erratic shifting from a faulty engine computer
issues.sym: Hard or jumpy shifts, flaring between gears, delayed engagement and a check engine light, sometimes ending in a transmission that stops working.
issues.why: The engine control module can malfunction and command the automatic transmission badly, which wears it out. Toyota extended warranty coverage on the module and transmission for these years.
issues.next: Have the computer and transmission diagnosed soon instead of driving on it, and ask a Toyota dealer whether any extended coverage still applies to your vehicle.

issues.sym: The oil level drops noticeably between changes, sometimes with blue smoke at startup or a low oil light.
issues.why: The oil control rings on the 2.4L engine do not scrape enough oil off the cylinder walls, so oil gets burned. Toyota addressed this with warranty enhancement ZE7.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and keep it topped up. Ask a Toyota dealer about the ZE7 program and have an oil consumption test done.

issues.t: Clunk or knock when turning the steering wheel
issues.sym: A clunking or clicking felt and heard through the steering wheel, most noticeable at low speed or turning on rough roads.
issues.why: The steering intermediate shaft wears and develops play. In some cases the steering rack itself needs attention.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft and rack inspected. Replacing the worn shaft usually cures the noise.

issues.t: Rear suspension arm can rust and separate
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the vehicle wandering or pulling, or uneven rear tire wear.
issues.why: Adjusting nuts on the rear suspension arms may have been tightened incorrectly during wheel alignment, letting the threads rust and the arm come loose. Toyota recalled these vehicles more than once and the final fix replaces both rear arms.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the rear arms replaced. Do not ignore new rear clunks or wandering.

issues.t: Accelerator can be trapped by the floor mat
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks down or will not return after pressing it.
issues.why: An unsecured or wrong-size driver floor mat can catch the pedal and hold it open. Toyota recalled these vehicles to modify the pedal and replace the mats.
issues.next: Remove any loose or stacked mats and check the VIN for open recalls. If the pedal ever sticks, shift to neutral and brake firmly.

issues.sym: The gas pedal feels stiff, comes back slowly, or stays partly pressed.
issues.why: A friction part inside the pedal assembly can become smooth and then grab when moisture condenses on it. Toyota recalled these years and added a reinforcement bar to the pedal.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and get the pedal fix. If the pedal sticks, shift to neutral and brake firmly.

issues.t: Driver power window switch can overheat
issues.sym: The window switch feels sticky or stops working, or there is a burning smell, smoke or melting near the driver door switch.
issues.why: Grease was applied inconsistently to the master window switch contacts at the factory, which can let the switch overheat. Toyota recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If you smell burning or see smoke from the door switch, stop and have it repaired before using it again.

issues.t: Airbag light from a damaged steering wheel cable
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working.
issues.why: A flat cable inside the steering column spiral cable can be damaged as the wheel is turned, which can stop the driver airbag from working. Toyota recalled these years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the spiral cable repaired. Treat an airbag light as a safety problem.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may deploy unexpectedly
issues.sym: Usually no warning beforehand. The airbag warning light may come on if a sensor has failed.
issues.why: Two roll-over sensors in the curtain airbag system can fail, and if both fail close together the curtain airbags and seat belt pretensioners could fire without a crash. Toyota recalled these years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the sensor assembly replaced.

issues.t: Rear outer seat belts can be cut in a crash
issues.sym: No symptom in daily driving. The problem only shows up in a severe frontal crash.
issues.why: In a frontal collision the rear outboard seat belts can be cut by the metal seat cushion frame. Toyota recalled these vehicles to add protective covers.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the protectors installed before carrying rear passengers.

issues.sym: The paint flakes or peels away in patches, often on the roof, hood or tailgate.
issues.why: Factory-applied Super White and Blizzard Pearl paint can lose adhesion. Toyota set up a customer support program with extended paint coverage for these colors.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer whether your vehicle and color are covered under the paint support program and have the peeling documented.

issues.sym: A shudder or vibration, like driving over rumble strips, during light acceleration at moderate speeds.
issues.why: The torque converter in the 6-speed automatic can shudder as it locks up. Toyota extended warranty coverage for it under program ZH1.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer road test it and check whether the ZH1 coverage applies to your vehicle.

issues.t: 12V battery can shift and short, risking fire
issues.sym: Usually no warning. A burning smell or smoke from under the hood is a sign to stop right away.
issues.why: Some replacement batteries are smaller than the original, and the hold-down clamp may not keep them in place. During hard cornering the battery can move and its positive terminal can touch the clamp, causing a short. Toyota recalled these years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the battery tray, hold-down and terminal cover replaced. Use the correct battery size when replacing it.

issues.t: Hesitation and lurching at low speed
issues.sym: A delay then a surge when pulling away, or jerky shifting in stop-and-go traffic.
issues.why: Shift behavior on the then-new 8-speed automatic. Toyota issued a service bulletin with updated transmission programming.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check for and install the latest transmission software (bulletin T-SB-0107-19).

issues.sym: Low coolant warning, the coolant level dropping with no obvious leak, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: Coolant loss is the most reported engine complaint on these years. Toyota also recalled some engines because tiny pores in the engine casting could crack and leak coolant inside or outside the engine.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the cooling system pressure-tested. Do not keep driving if the engine starts overheating.

issues.t: Front lower control arm can crack
issues.sym: Clunking from the front, odd steering feel, or the vehicle pulling. In the worst case a front wheel can come loose from the suspension.
issues.why: Some front lower suspension arms were made with a defect that lets them crack and separate. Toyota recalled a small number of vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have both front lower arms replaced before driving much further.

issues.t: Fuel tank will not fill completely
issues.sym: The pump clicks off early, the gauge does not show full after filling, and the distance-to-empty reading is shorter than expected.
issues.why: Variation in the fuel tank shape lets the fuel level sender tilt, so the tank fills short and the gauge reads low. Toyota offered coverage for repairs.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer about the refueling support bulletin for these years.

issues.t: Corroded high-voltage cable under the floor
issues.sym: A hybrid system warning on the dash, sometimes with reduced power. Rust is visible on the cable connections under the car.
issues.why: The high-voltage cable running under the floor to the rear motor can corrode early, especially where roads are salted. Toyota extended coverage on these cables for affected Hybrid models.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer inspect the high-voltage cable and ask about the extended cable coverage. Do not try to repair high-voltage parts yourself.
